record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: Compares correlated and uncorrelated initialization in CNNs and reports effects on training accuracy and convergence behavior, using a distinct initialization intervention and empirical setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-accuracy comparisons and gradient-dynamics results for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Its accuracy tables primarily report test accuracy; training-accuracy differences appear in text and plots. Theoretical claims about a single spatial filter are not additional benchmark-network results.
record.test_reason: The study compares initialization schemes and reports training dynamics and training accuracy, bearing on V4's initialization-dependent learning speed. Training accuracy also bears on V1, but the supplied text does not establish whether training error approaches zero.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that correlated initialization can accelerate training and improve generalization, with its benefits diminished by large learning rates and L2 regularization.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares correlated initialization derived from trained filter correlations with uncorrelated initialization; it does not test the original claim's random-label memorization recipe or directly establish near-zero classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization type, learning rate, L2-regularization, architecture, dataset, source correlation matrix and correlation strength affect reported accuracy or training dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Correlated initialization improves test accuracy across several architectures and datasets, with gains depending on learning rate, regularization, correlation source, and strength.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spatially correlated initialization can improve CNN generalization.

record.problems: Training-accuracy results are qualitative and largely figure-based; the numerical tables report accuracy without specifying that it is training accuracy. Each configuration uses 5 networks. The study does not report whether training classification error reaches zero or near zero.
record.rows_left_out: Test/generalization accuracy values in Tables 2–7 were omitted because they do not measure the training classification error named by V1. Gradient magnitude and sign-change results were also omitted because they do not measure the version's training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error is unresolved. Corrupted or random labels, Adam, model-size thresholds, early stopping, and the specified regularization-dependent failures are not tested.
Two-layer teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Activation-specific initialization comparisons, maximum trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in very deep tanh networks, and 10,000-layer plain CNN training.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Controlled normalization versus no-normalization comparisons and Fixup training speed or stability.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Missing absolute training-error values do not justify a V1 limits_scope verdict. The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plot values, so numerical endpoints cannot be inferred. V4 support concerns its learning-speed component only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training accuracy under correlated versus uncorrelated initialization, but not corrupted or random labels, Adam, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes with substantial remaining training error.
